summary.oneLiner: JTEKT India Limited is a tier-1 automotive component manufacturer supplying steering systems and driveline components on a business-to-business basis to Indian and overseas vehicle OEMs, with JTEKT Corporation, Japan as its holding company.
summary.business: The Company's main activity is manufacturing and assembling of automotive components, which the BRSR reports as 99.19% of turnover. Revenues are largely on a business-to-business basis to OEM customers as a tier 1 supplier, and the products described are steering systems, driveline components and similar items for passenger as well as commercial vehicles. Named OEM customers include Maruti Suzuki, TATA Motors, Honda, Toyota Kirloskar, Renault Nissan, Mahindra & Mahindra and Stellantis in India, alongside overseas accounts such as E-Z-Go Textron-USA, Trenton Pressing LLC-USA, JTEKT Brazil …

endMarkets: Indian passenger vehicle OEMs|Indian commercial vehicle OEMs|Exports, stated at 2.58% of total turnover, to customers in the USA, Brazil, Indonesia and France

currentContext.strengths: Tier-1 B2B position across a broad Indian OEM roster (Maruti Suzuki, TATA Motors, Honda, Toyota Kirloskar, Renault Nissan, Mahindra & Mahindra, Stellantis) rather than a single account|Technology access through the parent: JTEKT Corporation, Japan is the holding company, and related-party disclosures show royalty, technical support fee and receipt of services from it|Export channel into the JTEKT group network — supplies to JTEKT Brazil LTDA, PT. JTEKT Indonesia and JTEKT Column Systems France S.A.S|ICRA credit ratings reaffirmed at AA for long-term borrowings and A1+ for short-term borrowings|Falling employee churn — permanent employee turnover rate declined from 10.63% in FY 2023-24 to 8.77% in FY 2024-25 to 6.87% in FY 2025-26
currentContext.strategies: Drive efficiency across the manufacturing footprint through strategic rationalization — seven complex manufacturing rationalization projects (strategic consolidation, product line transfers, layout optimization) were completed during the year with five more underway|Embed the Kaizen philosophy as a structured approach to identify improvement opportunities and drive further rationalization across operations|Build a high-tech facility in Gujarat to increase customer proximity, slash logistics costs and ease supply chain risks in Western India|Digitise shop-floor operations — paperless Kanban-based material receipts, automated Pre-Dispatch Inspections (PDI) and interactive eGL boards tracking safety and energy metrics in real time|Strengthen prototyping capability and optimise product designs, prioritising innovation around evolving market dynamics and technical trends|Sustainable and ethical sourcing — front-loading activities, reduced part development lead times, the Supplier Parts Tracking Team (SPTT) system and regular Partners' Meets with supply-chain vendors|Move the seven manufacturing plants toward carbon neutrality and zero liquid discharge, anchored by an expanded 5,156 KWp solar infrastructure, with regular cybersecurity audits and carbon emission monitoring|Maintain stringent control over fixed costs, particularly employee and administrative expenses, to defend margin|People development under a 'Culture of Care' — training coverage, conversion of trainees into permanent roles and intake of fresh graduate and diploma trainees|The Company has no subsidiary — the BRSR reporting boundary is standalone because JTEKT India Ltd has no subsidiary company. Returns to shareholders are made through a final dividend paid out of the year's profit: the Board recommended a final dividend of INR 0.75 per equity share of INR 1 each for FY 2025-26 (against a rate of 70% on equity share capital in the previous financial year), with no amount carried to General Reserve, and the declaration is placed before members as ordinary business at the 42nd AGM on 26 August 2026. Related-party dealings with the holding company and with Maruti Suzuki India Limited are stated to be in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis, approved by the Audit Committee and the Board and within limits approved by members by ordinary resolution at the 41st AGM.|Renewable energy adoption through group captive solar and wind projects, open access power sourcing and rooftop solar installation, targeted at lower energy cost, a lower carbon footprint and carbon credit benefits|A carbon reduction roadmap with CO2 monitoring and energy efficiency projects to address rising energy costs and carbon regulation|Water recycling, rainwater harvesting, process optimisation and monitoring of water consumption per unit|Hazardous waste management through authorised disposal, waste segregation, reduction at source, vendor monitoring and awareness training|Alignment of the SHE (Safety, Health & Environment) Policy with global best practices, supported by a robust SHE management system, regular safety trainings and risk assessments, and promotion of mental health and ergonomic improvements|Machine safety enhancement programme — interlocks, guarding improvements, emergency stop systems, residual pressure control and safety automation|Grievance redressal mechanisms with published web links for communities, shareholders and employees/workers under the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct|CSR focused on quality education, healthcare including preventive healthcare, and training to promote rural sports, implemented in local areas after assessment of community requirements|Note on assurance: the BRSR states 'Not Applicable' for both the name of the assessment or assurance provider and the type of assurance obtained — the FY 2025-26 BRSR is unassured
currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26 the Company completed seven complex manufacturing rationalization projects covering strategic consolidation, product line transfers and layout optimization, with five additional projects underway; Kaizen is described as the structured approach used to identify further rationalization opportunities across operations. Crucially, the Company has commenced construction of a high-tech facility in Gujarat to increase customer proximity. No commissioning date, installed capacity or site-count detail for the new Gujarat facility is disclosed in the routed sections, and the Board's Report presents capital expenditure only as rupee amounts (excluded here as financial-statement figures).
currentContext.mdna: Record Indian automotive demand in FY 2025-26: passenger vehicles at 46.43 lakh units (7.9% growth), commercial vehicles recovering 12.6% to 10.80 lakh units, two-wheelers up 10.7% to 2.17 crore units and three-wheelers up 12.8% to 8.36 lakh units, with total production at 3.47 crore units|Management frames FY 2025-26 sales growth of 11% against 9% growth in the passenger vehicle market as evidence of consistent market-share gain|Margin lever is fixed-cost control: stringent control over employee and administrative expenses held the EBITDA margin at 7.5%, broadly in line with 7.6% in FY 2024-25, despite headwinds from rising raw material costs and higher interest expenses|Electrification: EV registrations crossed the 25 lakh unit threshold, up 24% year-on-year, driven by PM E-DRIVE, PLI localization and an expanding charging network, positioning the industry for a green mobility revolution|Macro backdrop — India's real GDP growth of 7.7% in 2025-26 with 2026-27 projected at 6.6%, against OECD global growth projected to slow from 3.4% in 2025 to 2.8% in 2026 before recovering to 3.1% in 2027|An above-normal monsoon at 108% of the Long Period Average revived rural liquidity and triggered robust demand for two-wheelers, tractors and small passenger cars; Union Budget tax-slab reform lifted middle-class disposable income|Structural shift to a fragmented, multi-polar trade order in which nations prioritise domestic supply chains and strategic autonomy; if supply chain and maritime bottlenecks stretch into 2027 global growth could take a further hit|Customer base concentrated in OEM partnerships — Maruti Suzuki, Mahindra & Mahindra, Tata Motors, Honda Cars India, Stellantis, Toyota Kirloskar, Club Car, E-z-go, Renault-Nissan, Isuzu, SML-Isuzu and Force Motors

risks.risk: Single-activity concentration on the automotive OEM cycle, overwhelmingly domestic
risks.note: The BRSR reports manufacturing and assembling of automotive components as 99.19% of turnover with exports contributing only 2.58% of total turnover, so nearly all revenue is tied to one activity and to Indian OEM demand; revenues are largely business-to-business to OEM customers as a tier 1 supplier.

Identified by the Company as a material issue: manufacturing activities involve operational hazards that may lead to injuries, production disruption and legal liabilities, with negative impact stated as medical expenses, compensation cost, production loss, legal liability and reputational damage. Mitigation is a stronger safety culture, KY activities, machine safeguarding, safety patrols, behaviour-based safety, training and audits.

Flagged as a material risk that may lead to accidents, injuries and production interruptions; mitigation is interlocks, guarding improvements, emergency stop systems, residual pressure control and safety automation, which itself carries investment and maintenance cost.

Listed as a material issue — standard of work may suffer on the exit of experienced employees, high turnover disrupts workflow and decreases productivity, and there is a high cost associated with recruiting, hiring and training replacements. Permanent worker turnover was 12.28% and permanent employee turnover 6.87% in FY 2025-26, both improved from 17.50% and 8.77% in FY 2024-25. Mitigation is robust succession planning for all critical roles and structured induction.

Contractor activities may introduce safety hazards, accidents and compliance issues, with accident liabilities, project delays and reputational impact as the stated downside; mitigated through contractor induction, permit systems, supervision, competency evaluation and audits.

Fire incidents may occur due to oils, electrical systems and hot work activities, with asset damage, downtime and insurance costs as the stated impact; mitigation is emergency drills, fire detection systems, hot work permits, firefighting training and regular inspections.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance with safety, health and environment laws
risks.note: Non-compliance with environmental, safety and labour regulations may result in penalties, legal actions and operational disruptions, including shutdown risk; mitigation is periodic compliance evaluations, internal audits, statutory monitoring, legal updates and training. The Board's Report separately notes the Company has a detailed Risk Management Policy that the Board periodically reviews.

risks.risk: Energy cost, carbon regulation and resource use (energy, water, hazardous waste)
risks.note: Rising energy costs and carbon regulations may increase operating costs; dependence on conventional energy sources adds carbon and regulatory pressure; water scarcity and stricter regulations may affect operations and increase costs; and improper handling or disposal of hazardous waste may cause environmental pollution and non-compliance with disposal costs, penalties and environmental liabilities.

one-line thesis: JTEKT India delivered 11% sales growth in FY26, outpacing the 9% PV market, driven by GST cuts boosting Maruti Suzuki volumes and new SOPs (e-Vitara/Victoris), though full-year EBITDA margins dipped 10bps to 7.5% due to adverse product mix (Honda decline) and accounting forex distortions. The thesis hinges on the rapid utilization of recently commissioned CVJ and Gear lines (currently under-utilized) and the successful ramp-up of exports to Brazil and the US, which should drive ROCE recovery from current depressed levels as CWIP converts to revenue-generating assets.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +11% YoY (outperforming market's 9%); EBITDA Margin: 7.5% (down 10bps YoY; H2 recovered to 8.48%); PAT: Impacted by forex accounting distortion (INR 62M cost) and US tariff (INR 63M); Order Book: Implicitly strong via new SOPs (Maruti MPV EV, Honda SUV); Net Debt: Increased due to INR 400Cr+ capex and Gujarat plant setup; One-offs: INR 8.2M rights issue expense, INR 62M forex accounting hit on imports, INR 63M US reciprocal tariff (now withdrawn).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Targeting ~INR 800Cr incremental revenue over next 1-2 years from capacity utilization; Margin: Expect improvement as product mix normalizes (Honda recovery) and high-margin CVJ/exports scale; Order Inflow: Brazil exports starting May '26 (70k units ramping to 500k); Capex: INR 250Cr total for Gujarat plant (INR 130Cr spent), remaining INR 100Cr+ in FY27.
order book & pipeline: New SOPs secured: Maruti Suzuki e-Vitara, Victoris, upcoming MPV EV (Oct '26); Honda SUV EV (Dec '26); Brazil export order (Stellantis) ramping from 70k to 500k units; CVJ capacity expanded to 7.54 lakh units (2 lines operational, 3rd coming).
segment / subsidiary detail: Steering (MS Gear): 60% of sales (up from 56%), strong growth from Alto, Jimny, Baleno; Driveline (CVJ): 5% of sales, currently INR 130Cr revenue, targeting INR 250Cr at 90% utilization; Exports: 3% of sales (up from 2%), US tariffs withdrawn, Brazil shipments commenced.
growth verticals / optionality: CVJ market share target of 15% (currently supplying Grand Vitara, Hyryder, e-Vitara, Victoris); Export expansion to Brazil (Stellantis) and renewed US opportunities; Honda business recovery with new EV SUV; Potential future driveline products (driveshafts) post-CVJ stabilization.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin pressure from product mix shift (low-margin Maruti models replaced high-margin Honda/Renault exports); Variable costs up 0.38% (power tariffs, US tariff, NPD costs); Fixed costs controlled (down 0.28% of sales); CVJ margins expected to be superior to MS Gear due to 100% localization.
capex / expansion: INR 400Cr+ in FY26; Major focus on Gujarat plant (INR 250Cr total, INR 130Cr spent); CVJ Line 2 commissioned Nov '25; MS Gear Lines 5 & 6, CPS Lines 3 & 4 added; CWIP stands at INR 411Cr, depressing current ROCE.
capital allocation: Successful maiden rights issue fully subscribed (Promoters + Public); Funds deployed for Gujarat plant and capacity expansion; Focus on converting CWIP to operating assets to improve ROCE (currently 10%, ex-CWIP ~11%, target >16%).
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration (Maruti Suzuki 60%); Delay in new model SOPs (Honda, Maruti MPV); Raw material price volatility (though pass-through exists); Execution risk on export ramp-up; Competition in CVJ segment (GKN, MTN).
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes strict cost control and temporary nature of margin headwinds (mix, forex accounting, tariffs); Confident on capacity utilization ramp-up driving ROCE recovery; Transparent on CWIP impact on ratios.
non-obvious takeaways: Accounting distortion: Forex gains on import payments booked as 'Other Income' rather than reducing material cost, artificially inflating material costs by INR 62M (0.23% margin impact); CVJ is 100% localized with no imports, offering better margin potential than imported-content steering gears; CWIP of INR 411Cr is a hidden asset not yet generating revenue, masking true operational efficiency.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
